statement.p: Alexis sells cars for a living, and earns 28\% of the dealerships sales profit as commission. In a certain month, she plans to earn \$2200 in commissions. How much total sales profit does she need to bring in for the dealership?
Alexis needs to bring in in sales profit.

solution.p: Be careful that you do not calculate 28\% of \$2200\text{.} That might be what a student would do who doesnt thoroughly read the question. If you have ever trained yourself to quickly find numbers in word problems and substitute them into formulas, you must unlearn this. The issue is that \$2200 is not the dealerships sales profit, and if you mistakenly multiply 0.28\cdot2200=616\text{,} then \$616 makes no sense as an answer to this question. How could Alexis bring in only \$616 of sales profit, and earn \$2200 in commission?

We can translate the problem into \$2200 is 28\% of what? Letting x be the sales profit for the dealership (in dollars), we can write and solve the equation: \begin{aligned} \pinover{2200}{\$2200}\amp\pinover{=}{is}\pinover{0.28}{28\%}\pinover{\cdot}{of}\pinover{x}{what}\\ \divideunder{2200}{0.28}\amp=\divideunder{0.28x}{0.28}\\ 7857.14\amp\approx x\\ x\amp\approx7857.14 \end{aligned} To earn \$2200 in commission, Alexis needs to bring in approximately \$7857.14 of sales profit for the dealership.
